prompt.context: Your client wants to understand the US pet food market. This is a market sizing and mental math exercise.
prompt.question: How large is the pet food market in the US? What information would you need?

clarifying_info.q: Can you provide data on pet ownership rates in the US?
How many dogs are in the US?
clarifying_info.a: See Exhibit 2 (provided when asked for dog-count data).

clarifying_info.q: How much food do dogs eat per day?
clarifying_info.a: See Exhibit 3 — feeding guidelines by breed.

clarifying_info.q: What does dog food cost at various retailers?
clarifying_info.a: See Exhibit 4 — store audit price data.

clarifying_info.q: How many customers does Safeway / Walmart have?
clarifying_info.a: Safeway has approximately 10M yearly customers; Walmart has approximately 100M yearly customers.

clarifying_info.q: What share of Safeway / Walmart customers have dogs?
clarifying_info.a: You can assume 40% of customers have dogs (consistent with Exhibit 1).

clarifying_info.q: What share of dog-owning customers buy dog food at Safeway / Walmart?
clarifying_info.a: Assume 10% of customers who have dogs buy their dog food at the respective retailer.

exhibits.title: Pet Ownership Rates in US (2015)
exhibits.shows: Bar or table chart showing the percentage of US households that own various types of pets, sourced from a 2015 consumer survey.
exhibits.data: Approximately 58% of US households own at least one pet; ~40% own dogs; ~33% own cats (read from chart).

exhibits.title: Number of Dogs & Cats in Pet-Owning Households (2015)
exhibits.shows: Distribution of dog-owning households by number of dogs (1, 2-3, 4+), sourced from a 2015 consumer survey.
exhibits.data: Among dog-owning households: 58% have 1 dog, 36% have 2-3 dogs, 7% have 4+ dogs.

exhibits.title: Feeding Guidelines for Various Dog and Cat Breeds (Dry Food, Ounces/Day)
exhibits.shows: Table listing recommended daily dry food intake in ounces for several dog breeds and cat breeds. Note: 16 ounces per pound.
exhibits.data: Dog breed ounces/day (five data points): 4, 8, 14, 17, 32. Cat breed ounces/day also listed.

exhibits.title: Store Audit — Pet Food Prices
exhibits.shows: List of dog and cat food products with their retail price and package weight from various store channels.
exhibits.data: Cat: Friskies Seafood Sensations (PetSmart) 16 lbs $11.99. Dog: Ol' Roy (Walmart) 40 lbs $18.97; Kibbles 'n Bits (Safeway) 17.6 lbs $13.49; Eukanuba (PetSmart) 40 lbs $39.99; Blue Buffalo (Independent) 33 lbs $49.99.

framework: Start with US population (~320M) and derive number of households (320M / 3.2 = 100M)
Apply pet ownership rate from Exhibit 1 (~58%) to find households with pets
Estimate average number of pets per pet-owning household (~1.5) to get total pet count
Estimate annual food consumption per pet (bags per month × price per bag)
Calculate total market revenue: pet count × annual spend per pet
Optionally segment by species (dog vs. cat) for greater precision

questions.prompt: How many dogs are there in the US? (Use Exhibit 2)
questions.guidance: Candidate should start from 100M US households, apply 40% dog-ownership rate (Exhibit 1), then use the 1/2-3/4+ distribution from Exhibit 2 to compute a weighted total dog count. A strong answer multiplies each tier by an assumed average number of dogs in that tier.

math.setup: 100M households × 40% = 40M dog-owning households. Split by tier using Exhibit 2 percentages and multiply by assumed dogs per household.

questions.prompt: What is the market for dog food in the US? (Use Exhibits 3 and 4)
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute average daily ounce consumption across dog breeds from Exhibit 3, convert to pounds, annualize, then derive a per-pound price from Exhibit 4 and multiply. Rounding is encouraged.

math.setup: Average daily consumption from Exhibit 3 dog data (5 values: 4, 8, 14, 17, 32 oz). Average price per pound from Exhibit 4 dog products (4 items).
steps: Annual consumption per dog: 1 lb/day × 360 days = 360 lbs/year

questions.prompt: What is the yearly demand for dog food at Walmart and Safeway? (Use Exhibit 4 and additional assumptions)
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply the 40% dog-ownership rate to each retailer's customer base, then apply 10% purchase-at-retailer assumption, compute bags purchased per year using annual 360 lb consumption and package sizes, and convert to revenue. Note: Walmart uses its store brand (Ol' Roy 40 lbs $18.97); Safeway uses Kibbles 'n Bits (17.6 lbs $13.49). Rounding encouraged.

math.setup: Safeway: 10M customers. Walmart: 100M customers. 40% have dogs. 10% of dog owners buy dog food at that retailer. Annual consumption = 360 lbs/dog.
math.answer: Safeway: ~7.2M bags/year, ~$108M revenue. Walmart: ~36M bags/year, ~$720M revenue.

recommendation: The US pet food market is approximately $19B per year in dog food alone, underpinned by ~70M dogs and ~$270 annual spend per dog.
Walmart commands far larger volume (36M bags vs 7.2M for Safeway) due to its 10x larger customer base.
risks: Assumptions about average dog size and food consumption may skew results; premium vs. economy mix shifts the price average significantly.
10% dog-food purchase rate at a given retailer is a simplifying assumption; actual channel share varies.
next_steps: Extend analysis to cat food and other pet categories to size the full US pet food market.
Segment by retail channel (grocery, mass, pet specialty, e-commerce) to identify growth pockets.
Validate assumptions with syndicated market data (e.g., Euromonitor, Nielsen).
